title: To Jordan Came Our Lord, the Christ
description: To Jordan Came Our Lord, the Christ in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Martin Luther, first published in 1541. The English translation is by Richard Massie (1854). The tune, CHRIST, UNSER HERR, is by Johann Walther (1524). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: To Jor-dan came our Lord the Christ, To do God's plea-sure will_-ing, And there was by Saint John bap-tized, All right-eous-ness ful-fill_-ing; There did He con-se-crate a bath To wash a-way trans-gres__-sion, And quench the bit-ter-ness of death By His own blood and pas__-sion; He would a new life give_ us.

lines: To Jordan came our Lord the Christ,
And there was by Saint John baptized,
There did He consecrate a bath
And quench the bitterness of death
By His own blood and passion;
He would a new life give us.
So hear ye all, and well perceive
And what a Christian should believe
That we should water use, the Lord
Not simple water, but the Word
To show us this, He hath His Word
On Jordan's banks was plainly heard
Hear Him." Yea, hear Him every one
The Holy Ghost from Heaven's gate
That thus the truth be not denied,
Nor should our faith e'er waver,
That the Three Persons all preside,
That lost in sin they must repent;
He that believes and is baptized,
A newborn man, no more he dies,
